0129208b7a788cf8ef7897a2656495e9.jpg.t: The stairway, cut from the passage itself
0129208b7a788cf8ef7897a2656495e9.jpg.what: “A House in Memory” — cut-up word strips arranged into the shape of a house
0129208b7a788cf8ef7897a2656495e9.jpg.mech: Words cut from a book and physically arranged into the outline of the thing the book is about. Form and content are the same object.
0129208b7a788cf8ef7897a2656495e9.jpg.ours: Every word of Genesis 28 cut into paper strips and laid as a staircase rising off the bottom-left corner — each step a phrase, treads shortening as they climb, some strips upside down. Real scissors, real shadows, photographed flat. The text becomes the ladder.
0129208b7a788cf8ef7897a2656495e9.jpg.where: Cover candidate, or the poster page

10c8b432a4df733f3df36d7369dd645e.jpg.what: Weekly Bingo for tiny achievements · January's Inner Work — a hand-drawn grid you circle
10c8b432a4df733f3df36d7369dd645e.jpg.mech: Things too small to count as achievements, which is exactly why ticking them feels good. It becomes yours the moment you mark it.
10c8b432a4df733f3df36d7369dd645e.jpg.ours: Twenty-five squares of ordinary faithfulness nobody claps for: told the truth when a lie was easier · let someone go first · said sorry first · didn't say the thing · read one verse · sat with somebody who was sad · asked for help. Free square in the middle: you woke up.

0321d6f53d422918ff5cadc5f429ec5d.jpg.t: A person made entirely of text
0321d6f53d422918ff5cadc5f429ec5d.jpg.what: #91 — a portrait collaged from strips of a biography, the figure cut out of the words that describe him
0321d6f53d422918ff5cadc5f429ec5d.jpg.mech: The person and the account of the person are the same material. You cannot look at the man without reading about him.
0321d6f53d422918ff5cadc5f429ec5d.jpg.ours: A human silhouette assembled from strips of Psalm 139 — every strip a phrase about being known, seen, formed, counted. The figure is cut out of the text and stands on a plain road. Nothing drawn; everything cut.
0321d6f53d422918ff5cadc5f429ec5d.jpg.where: A full page, or a Spine cover

07e996f902f308b7128abdab4e897948.jpg.t: 20 sentences people think are in the Bible
07e996f902f308b7128abdab4e897948.jpg.what: #94 — “20 Sentences In 60 Seconds That Will Change Your Life”, highlighter over printed lines
07e996f902f308b7128abdab4e897948.jpg.mech: A numbered list with a promise of speed, marked up in yellow so it reads like somebody already studied it for you.
07e996f902f308b7128abdab4e897948.jpg.ours: Twenty sentences, fifteen genuinely in the Bible and five that absolutely are not — “God helps those who help themselves”, “God won't give you more than you can handle”, “money is the root of all evil”. The five fakes highlighted in a different colour and corrected in the margin. This page makes us trustworthy by admitting what gets misquoted, including by us.

095e2cc0819b961a5f3f369a4c391ab1.jpg.what: #97 — fixed vs growth mindset drawn as the identical four puzzle pieces, once locked shut and once open
095e2cc0819b961a5f3f369a4c391ab1.jpg.mech: One object drawn twice, with only one property changed. The whole argument is in the difference, and no sentence is needed.
095e2cc0819b961a5f3f369a4c391ab1.jpg.ours: The identical rock drawn twice, same size, same shading. Labelled A PILLOW and A PILLAR. Nothing about the stone changed between the two drawings — only the night in between, and what he did with it in the morning.

116cb1d50872c221a38d887d951d7c12.jpg.what: #102 — a postbox on a wall beside a rack of tear-off cards: leave your impression behind, drop the card in
116cb1d50872c221a38d887d951d7c12.jpg.mech: Two actions, not one. You take something AND you give something back, anonymously, and the wall keeps both.
116cb1d50872c221a38d887d951d7c12.jpg.ours: Stronger than the tear-off page on its own. A perforated strip of notes to take, and directly beside it a card to fill in and post back — the address printed on it. What comes back becomes page 28 of the next issue. The paper stops being a broadcast.
116cb1d50872c221a38d887d951d7c12.jpg.where: Its own page, near the Spine

1759d89e82d01827b72a26f9e617efd7.jpg.what: #103 — The Creative Manifesto: hand-lettered centred lines inside a thick wobbling blue border
1759d89e82d01827b72a26f9e617efd7.jpg.mech: The wobble is the whole personality. A straight frame would make it corporate; the hand-drawn one makes it a gift.
1759d89e82d01827b72a26f9e617efd7.jpg.ours: Same treatment for the twelve-line Between Sundays manifesto — hand-lettered, centred, inside a wobbling border in one of our inks. Every line is a verse in plain speech with its reference set tiny underneath. It is designed to be torn out and stuck on a wall.

db0ac0f36a66a4b782b0223471021ccf.jpg.what: Le Cafetier cover (draft) — cream stock, Didone nameplate, red only for labels, teasers top and bottom
db0ac0f36a66a4b782b0223471021ccf.jpg.mech: Four teasers above the fold and four below, each with a section label and page number. The cover works as a menu, not a poster.
db0ac0f36a66a4b782b0223471021ccf.jpg.ours: Already answered — our Issue 001 cover uses this exact skeleton: nameplate, teaser strips top and bottom, one big middle moment. Keep this piece as the cover's control reference.

da3252892dc1a9966a31b4a24e66d7e6.jpg.t: The paper inside its own picture
da3252892dc1a9966a31b4a24e66d7e6.jpg.what: Le Cafetier cover (final) — full-bleed illustration, headline inside it, the paper drawn into its own scene
da3252892dc1a9966a31b4a24e66d7e6.jpg.mech: The publication appears inside its own illustration — a wink the reader finds later. Ownership without a logo lockup.
da3252892dc1a9966a31b4a24e66d7e6.jpg.ours: Somewhere in Issue 002's cover art, a copy of Between Sundays sits on a table in the scene. A standing tradition readers learn to hunt for — our little 'certain place' in every cover.

ece4756d4530465af2755fa776db2b28.jpg.what: Arkitektnytt — same skeleton every issue, a single spot colour rotated per issue
ece4756d4530465af2755fa776db2b28.jpg.mech: The system IS the identity; the colour is the only variable. Instantly collectible on a shelf.
ece4756d4530465af2755fa776db2b28.jpg.ours: Issue 001 is butter. Issue 002 is sky. Issue 003 is sage. The nameplate never changes; collectors see the row of spines change colour. Cheap to print, strong on a rack.

676285db6fc3f78f8312490fcd7e9bae.jpg.what: Troika inside spread — coloured section word in the folio, duotone illustration, five hard columns
676285db6fc3f78f8312490fcd7e9bae.jpg.mech: Colour carries wayfinding only; the density is comfortable because the hierarchy is ruthless.
676285db6fc3f78f8312490fcd7e9bae.jpg.ours: Already the control reference for The Reading (pages 07–13, built). Keep.

fd68c2962cb4554b2f0a1e5ad545e213.jpg.what: Redbook 'Calm your life' — one illustration, the headline set INSIDE it, body starts halfway down
fd68c2962cb4554b2f0a1e5ad545e213.jpg.mech: The image is the layout. Type submits to the picture instead of sitting above it.
fd68c2962cb4554b2f0a1e5ad545e213.jpg.ours: For the 'morning after' feature (p14): the headline set into the empty sky of the artwork, body entering late. Rule 7 in the DNA doc.

aff1f90a110f234ef47d5101ce9e7157.jpg.what: 'Journal' template cover — coloured teaser cards under a nameplate
aff1f90a110f234ef47d5101ce9e7157.jpg.mech: A negative example: the colour blocks carry no information, so it reads as a template.
aff1f90a110f234ef47d5101ce9e7157.jpg.ours: Keep as the what-not-to-do reference beside the DNA rule: colour is information (section, folio, jump) or it goes.
aff1f90a110f234ef47d5101ce9e7157.jpg.skipwhy: Negative example — kept to teach the rule

0e171679fc143970789589d5155ec06a.jpg.what: Die Zeit front — one huge illustration owns the page; the article floats in a white panel on top
0e171679fc143970789589d5155ec06a.jpg.mech: Confidence: give the page to the image, then float the words on it.
0e171679fc143970789589d5155ec06a.jpg.ours: Already used on p07 (the 'Before you read' panel). Keep as the loud-page control.

54e7fecaccd2a40f7ea3002106eb3113.jpg.what: Barcelona indie — a full poster page facing dense text plus a rail of tiny ads
54e7fecaccd2a40f7ea3002106eb3113.jpg.mech: The spread contrast IS the design. One shout, one murmur.
54e7fecaccd2a40f7ea3002106eb3113.jpg.ours: The paper's spread law (DNA rule 1). Every spread we ship gets checked against this image.

2f3e505edb42d9ed85c54d74ecb31473.jpg.t: The brand paper that stays a paper
2f3e505edb42d9ed85c54d74ecb31473.jpg.what: The Snack Break — a joke newspaper that never breaks format
2f3e505edb42d9ed85c54d74ecb31473.jpg.mech: Humour lives inside the discipline. The format is never the punchline.
2f3e505edb42d9ed85c54d74ecb31473.jpg.ours: Our obituaries/coupons/classifieds pages obey this: the joke is in the content, the furniture stays dead straight.

b1803e4f52380e8c713b8b9535d2f214.jpg.what: NYT Sunday Review — flat coral field, illustration over it, two stacked drop-cap stories, a question resting inside the art
b1803e4f52380e8c713b8b9535d2f214.jpg.mech: Colour as ground, not decoration. A question set in a lighter tint gives the eye a rest stop.
b1803e4f52380e8c713b8b9535d2f214.jpg.ours: The single best reference in the library — the control for our loud pages. The 'question to carry' boxes come from here.

c8628a04bca259c163d6d6914fd114d8.jpg.what: Boston Globe Books — illustrated scene + giant numeral up top, five columns of dense listings below
c8628a04bca259c163d6d6914fd114d8.jpg.mech: The eye gets somewhere to stand first; then density is comfortable.
c8628a04bca259c163d6d6914fd114d8.jpg.ours: The control for the directory (p34, built) and any listing page. A giant numeral locked into art = the entry point.

0a40cc870154a6d0c3e15875a7e7f834.jpg.t: Two bands, headline in the middle
0a40cc870154a6d0c3e15875a7e7f834.jpg.what: Süddeutsche — illustration bands top AND bottom, text between, headline dropped mid-page
0a40cc870154a6d0c3e15875a7e7f834.jpg.mech: A completely different rhythm from hero-image-on-top. The middle of the page becomes the loudest place.
0a40cc870154a6d0c3e15875a7e7f834.jpg.ours: For a Reading interior page in Issue 002: the stairway crossing the top band, the sleepers at the bottom, the verses running between heaven and earth. The layout enacts Genesis 28:12.

eba208231c1e5f3290f847d31428d042.jpg.t: One diagonal object breaks the grid
eba208231c1e5f3290f847d31428d042.jpg.what: Chosun Weekly Biz — a cut-out ship laid diagonally across the columns, text wrapping its hull
eba208231c1e5f3290f847d31428d042.jpg.mech: The grid reads stronger for being broken exactly once.
eba208231c1e5f3290f847d31428d042.jpg.ours: The field-guide explainer (p17): one object (the stone, actual size) laid diagonally across the columns with the text wrapping it. Once per issue, never twice.

327040cc0b2fc5105440821842376e58.jpg.t: Cut-out figure on a team-colour field
327040cc0b2fc5105440821842376e58.jpg.what: Packers Preview — cut-out player, stacked caps headline in the negative space, stats rail
327040cc0b2fc5105440821842376e58.jpg.mech: Flat colour field + silhouette + headline stacked into the empty half. Sports-page DNA.
327040cc0b2fc5105440821842376e58.jpg.ours: Already the control for p19 Away Team Advantage (built). The stats rail pattern also feeds the printer-brief style tables.

ece34814e7f83ce3814f592351b184f9.jpg.what: Ciclismo Epico — an entire illustrated newspaper about one subject (cycling, ten stories, decades apart), with an index, champions column, glossary teaser
ece34814e7f83ce3814f592351b184f9.jpg.mech: One obsession treated with full newspaper seriousness. The index of ten stories IS the front page's promise.
ece34814e7f83ce3814f592351b184f9.jpg.ours: This is Between Sundays' own proof-of-concept in another category — one chapter of Genesis given a whole paper. Steal two parts: the numbered 'In questa edizione' index as our contents treatment, and the 'i nostri campioni' rail — ours becomes 'The cast of Genesis 28' (Jacob, Esau, Isaac, Rebekah, the angels, the stone) each with one line and a page number.

cdde1f567ea8d3fde28b257aced0f9af.jpg.what: Washington Post Health & Science — a labelled special section inside a real paper: banner, four teasers, one big illustrated feature with a question headline
cdde1f567ea8d3fde28b257aced0f9af.jpg.mech: A section-within-the-paper gets its own flag and colour world, and the lead headline is a QUESTION ('Too old to practice?').
cdde1f567ea8d3fde28b257aced0f9af.jpg.ours: The Reading gets a section flag treated exactly like this — 'THE READING · SPECIAL SECTION' with its own banner and a question lead: 'What do you do when it gets dark?' Question headlines belong to us; Jesus asked 300.

375eb887d5e6918aa9c1fa3f9f102ef0-1.jpg.what: Marc Maron tour poster — halftone portrait, checklists, testimonials, coupon corner, a signature block, every inch working
375eb887d5e6918aa9c1fa3f9f102ef0-1.jpg.mech: Vintage handbill density played straight. The checklist and the fill-in coupon make it interactive without being cute.
375eb887d5e6918aa9c1fa3f9f102ef0-1.jpg.ours: The Supply Co page (p41) upgraded to this energy: halftone stone 'product' photo, spirited testimonials ('slept on it — Jacob, Beersheba'), a MARON-style checklist ('CHECK ALL THAT APPLY: tired · running · unqualified · awake'), and a clip-out order form for things that cost $0.

09efd5f4e80642b12dc0808f9337c4ed.jpg.what: Information (Denmark) — 'Hvad må et liv koste…?': one dark illustration bridging the gutter, one lit figure, a timeline strip underneath
09efd5f4e80642b12dc0808f9337c4ed.jpg.mech: The spread is one picture; the timeline underneath grounds the emotion in fact. One small lit figure carries the whole page.
09efd5f4e80642b12dc0808f9337c4ed.jpg.ours: The Reading's night spread: the dark field across both pages, one small lit sleeper at the gutter, and underneath a factual strip — the timeline of the journey (Beersheba, day one … Haran, month later) in agate. Emotion above, geography below.
09efd5f4e80642b12dc0808f9337c4ed.jpg.where: Pages 10–11 rebuild as a true spread

4fb4f00da281816f6b80e7846a1b0aaf-1.jpg.t: The forest that owns the page
4fb4f00da281816f6b80e7846a1b0aaf-1.jpg.what: NYT Sunday Review — 'Rethinking the Wild': illustration fills everything, headline sits low inside it, body waits at the bottom
4fb4f00da281816f6b80e7846a1b0aaf-1.jpg.mech: The picture is allowed to be 75% of the page; the headline enters LATE, near the bottom third.
4fb4f00da281816f6b80e7846a1b0aaf-1.jpg.ours: For 'The place you almost walked past' (p15): the ordinary town of Luz drawn dense as that forest, one unnoticed clearing at the centre, headline low: 'Nobody in this drawing saw anything.'

3575e24fdfb02100d149e89054e316a2.jpg.what: Star-Ledger Sports 'SPLIT DECISION' — one player mirrored left/right, before/after stat rails on each side, tracked-out headline between
3575e24fdfb02100d149e89054e316a2.jpg.mech: Symmetry as argument: same man, two eras, stats flanking. The body text runs down the seam.
3575e24fdfb02100d149e89054e316a2.jpg.ours: Jacob, mirrored: left side 'BEERSHEBA' (what he had: a stolen blessing, a death threat, a rock) vs right side 'BETHEL +20 YEARS' (two camps, twelve sons, a limp, a new name) — stat-rail style, story down the middle. Sports-page rigor applied to Genesis 28 vs Genesis 32.

2a4c33143233bfafc3a004095e4f36d1.jpg.what: ELLE Decoration 'Pick of Pimlico Road' — an illustrated winding street with real shops, each entry keyed to a building
2a4c33143233bfafc3a004095e4f36d1.jpg.mech: The map and the listings are one drawing. You read the street by walking it with your eyes.
2a4c33143233bfafc3a004095e4f36d1.jpg.ours: 'The road to Haran' as an illustrated winding route — each stop a listing written like a shop entry: Beersheba (family business, recently left), the unnamed field (vacancies nightly, one rock provided), Luz (nothing to see here, locals say), Bethel (under new name). Geography as a directory page.

0419231d742eef55bd4ce9a9c5755fdd.jpg.t: The links-page as a front page
0419231d742eef55bd4ce9a9c5755fdd.jpg.what: Il Mestiere — a weekly that curates OTHER people's work as newspaper items, every story tagged with its source in brackets
0419231d742eef55bd4ce9a9c5755fdd.jpg.mech: Curation played straight as news. Each block credits its source like a wire tag.
0419231d742eef55bd4ce9a9c5755fdd.jpg.ours: 'The week in the Word' — a curation page where every item is something FOUND: a verse somebody sent in, a lyric that quotes scripture, a church sign, a tweet-length testimony — each tagged [PSALM 121] [SENT BY A READER] [SEEN ON HWY 280]. The paper as aggregator of where God showed up this week.

a470050aac489d89ebe5f343ff25c00d.jpg.what: 'Bad-Neighbor Blues' — one brick wall, two windows, smoke from one falling as rain on the other; text wraps the art
a470050aac489d89ebe5f343ff25c00d.jpg.mech: Two people who never meet share one wall; the illustration carries the relationship the text describes.
a470050aac489d89ebe5f343ff25c00d.jpg.ours: 'The neighbour you never met' — Luz upstairs asleep, Jacob downstairs dreaming; same wall, one night. Or modern: two apartments, one person praying, one person crying, one wall between. Ends with the directory pointer: someone within ten feet of you is on page 34.

fa0818b97e5cf331e1d274a8e8f35bd3.jpg.what: 'City of the News' — a lorem-ipsum newspaper template: the furniture without any content
fa0818b97e5cf331e1d274a8e8f35bd3.jpg.mech: A caution: all the newspaper furniture with nothing true inside it. Exactly what AI slop looks like in print.
fa0818b97e5cf331e1d274a8e8f35bd3.jpg.ours: Keep as the second negative reference beside the 'colour as decoration' one. This is what our pages must never be — structure imitated, nothing sourced.

1bfe255dd506c59defb9ecf95569ab6e.jpg.what: Süddeutsche Gesellschaft 'Gut gebucht' — a massive stacked crowd of faces balancing over one person reading at a desk
1bfe255dd506c59defb9ecf95569ab6e.jpg.mech: Scale inversion: the enormous thing (everyone) rests on the small thing (one person and a book).
1bfe255dd506c59defb9ecf95569ab6e.jpg.ours: One person reading this paper at a kitchen table, and stacked above them, drawn as one teetering crowd: everyone in the story — Jacob, Esau, Rebekah, Laban, the angels, the whole genealogy. Caption: 'Everyone in this drawing was somebody's ordinary Tuesday once.' The Bible's crowd balancing on one reader's attention.

0dc9f5057a9a4524025d9047cee8cd36.jpg.what: The Happy News — hand-lettered positive newspaper photographed in someone's hands outdoors
0dc9f5057a9a4524025d9047cee8cd36.jpg.mech: Proof-of-life photography: the paper exists, someone is holding it in daylight. The product shot IS a person reading.
0dc9f5057a9a4524025d9047cee8cd36.jpg.ours: Not a page — a marketing law. Every BTS promo photo is the paper IN HANDS, outdoors, being read: porch, bus stop, break room. Never a flat product render. Feeds the Grow playbook and the 'where this paper went' page (p46).

a1fd2e7d732b8bbc2b03d91c02f9c9c9.jpg.what: 'Mar de Plástico' — a full-page data poster: stencil headline, one big illustrated object, real counted numbers everywhere, source line at the foot
a1fd2e7d732b8bbc2b03d91c02f9c9c9.jpg.mech: Counted facts presented with print-shop rawness. The numbers are the drama; the texture keeps it human.
a1fd2e7d732b8bbc2b03d91c02f9c9c9.jpg.ours: 'The Census of One Night' — Genesis 28 counted like fieldwork: 1 traveller · 0 companions · ~800 km to go · 1 stone · 13 verses · 2 directions of traffic on the stairway · 0 conditions attached · 20 years until he returns · 1 name changed. Every figure straight from the text with its verse cited. Data journalism where the dataset is scripture.
a1fd2e7d732b8bbc2b03d91c02f9c9c9.jpg.where: Field guide alternate (p17) — strongest infographic play we have

d6707ec0025c957a2c1145b6be25fd01.jpg.what: American Way 'Moneypenny, Get Me Eurostar' — travel feature with a panoramic illustrated train window and a voice-driven column
d6707ec0025c957a2c1145b6be25fd01.jpg.mech: The illustration is one long window; the prose is personality-first service journalism.
d6707ec0025c957a2c1145b6be25fd01.jpg.ours: 'The 800-Kilometre Walk' as a travel review: Beersheba to Haran rated like a route — walking time, lodging (one field, unstaffed), amenities (a rock), what previous travellers say. Deadpan travel-desk voice over the deepest journey in Genesis.

46047ce7640d7bcf3159d0c99ebd5e75-1.jpg.what: 'Mother Knows Best — Except When You're Traveling' — numbered cultural etiquette lessons, each with a spot illustration
46047ce7640d7bcf3159d0c99ebd5e75-1.jpg.mech: Numbered small lessons, each getting its own drawing; the page teaches without lecturing because it stays concrete.
46047ce7640d7bcf3159d0c99ebd5e75-1.jpg.ours: 'Church, for people who haven't been in a while' — five numbered etiquette notes, honest and warm: nobody checks your attendance record · you can sit at the back on purpose · you don't need the right clothes · people will say 'good to see you' and mean it · you're allowed to leave before the end. Each with a spot drawing. The most practical page we could give the Quiet Seeker.
46047ce7640d7bcf3159d0c99ebd5e75-1.jpg.where: New page candidate — near the directory

0b2b982f580ac5a237edf929b03b74c8.jpg.what: IKEA Illustrator '22 — a whole life laid out flat, every object labelled with deadpan captions
0b2b982f580ac5a237edf929b03b74c8.jpg.mech: Knolling with a voice: every object named and captioned, the joke living in the labels.
0b2b982f580ac5a237edf929b03b74c8.jpg.ours: 'Everything Jacob Packed' laid out flat: the clothes he stood in (caption: all of it) · a stolen blessing (does not fit in a bag) · directions from his mother (verbal) · no food, no tent, no plan. Then one addition at the bottom of the page: a promise he didn't pack — 'I am with you' — labelled ACQUIRED IN TRANSIT.
0b2b982f580ac5a237edf929b03b74c8.jpg.where: Page 05 rebuild — this beats the current baggage-claim page

119dcb5f8cf19eb73e2a909820e5adba.jpg.what: 'Foods That Shouldn't Taste Good, But…Do?' — a service page reviewing things that sound wrong but work
119dcb5f8cf19eb73e2a909820e5adba.jpg.mech: The headline names the reader's scepticism first, then the entries earn trust one by one.
119dcb5f8cf19eb73e2a909820e5adba.jpg.ours: 'Verses that shouldn't comfort anybody, but…do' — the hard passages people actually cling to: Jesus weeping (John 11:35), 'my God, why have you abandoned me' (Matthew 27:46), Job wishing he'd never been born (Job 3:3). Reviewed like the food page: why it sounds wrong, why it lands. Honest about the strange parts of the Book.

12a8db50241e5e70039afe48ac6368aa.jpg.what: Wooden Toy Music Edition — a two-colour letterpress event poster: rules, ribbons, starbursts, every fact shouted
12a8db50241e5e70039afe48ac6368aa.jpg.mech: Two inks, total conviction. Density that never muddies because everything sits in a ruled box.
12a8db50241e5e70039afe48ac6368aa.jpg.ours: 'ONE NIGHT ONLY — A FIELD OUTSIDE LUZ' — the events poster for the dream: special appearance by the angels of God (both directions) · doors at sundown · admission free · no one awake for the performance. Two-ink letterpress voice, played completely straight.

150bf5f8ad768e39d1533a5259bc0200.jpg.what: A grid of 35 vintage cereal boxes — every one shouting FREE INSIDE, NEW!, a prize
150bf5f8ad768e39d1533a5259bc0200.jpg.mech: Repetition of a commercial format until the format itself becomes the subject. Every box promises a prize inside.
150bf5f8ad768e39d1533a5259bc0200.jpg.ours: 'FREE INSIDE' — a page of drawn cereal-box fronts, every box a promise from scripture played as breakfast marketing: MERCY-O'S (new every morning!) · REST FLAKES (come to me, all who are weary) · DAILY BREAD (give us this day). Each box carries its verse where the nutrition panel goes. One box in the corner, plain: THE REAL THING — free, no purchase necessary, John 4:14.
150bf5f8ad768e39d1533a5259bc0200.jpg.where: Full page — the funnest page in the paper

1a9c309e6aabfc45f5aacd61e9889f89.jpg.t: The venue that prints its own paper
1a9c309e6aabfc45f5aacd61e9889f89.jpg.what: A Central BH — a cultural venue's own letterpress newspaper: blackletter nameplate, illustrated lead, ribbon dividers, event listings as news
1a9c309e6aabfc45f5aacd61e9889f89.jpg.mech: An institution narrating itself in newspaper form; the format grants seriousness to small local events.
1a9c309e6aabfc45f5aacd61e9889f89.jpg.ours: The model for churches: a one-sheet BTS local edition any congregation can fill in — their events set like news, their people like columnists, our chassis carrying it. The distribution product the Local Church Nano persona hands out. 'Your church, printed like it matters.'

78996e2b52ee0c69144e97da328f67af.jpg.ours: Control for THE STONE radial (already concepted). One addition from seeing it properly: the two halves are TITLED — one side 'one man's trash', the other 'another's treasure'. Ours titles the halves A PILLOW / A PILLAR, so the radial argument has an axis.

7a11506dea4d638a04b9b1af277c6c38.jpg.what: 'The Cultural Iceberg' — visible culture above the waterline, deep culture below
7a11506dea4d638a04b9b1af277c6c38.jpg.mech: The waterline splits the seen from the unseen.
7a11506dea4d638a04b9b1af277c6c38.jpg.ours: Skip for the paper as-is (classroom infographic), but the WATERLINE mechanic is worth holding: what people see of a believer (Sunday, the habits) vs what carries it underneath (the doubts, the discipline, the kept promises). If it ever runs, it's drawn as our own object — not an iceberg.
7a11506dea4d638a04b9b1af277c6c38.jpg.skipwhy: Classroom-infographic genre; keep the waterline idea, not the page

7b990f1597ea785d36a8284c7e0ce90e.jpg.t: The raft on a sea of words
7b990f1597ea785d36a8284c7e0ce90e.jpg.what: A tiny photographed figure on a raft, floating on an ocean made of thousands of cut newspaper fragments
7b990f1597ea785d36a8284c7e0ce90e.jpg.mech: Scale contrast: one real person adrift on infinite chopped-up language. The sea is literally made of noise.
7b990f1597ea785d36a8284c7e0ce90e.jpg.ours: 'ALL THE ADVICE' — one small figure on a raft, and the entire sea is cut-up fragments of everything the world tells you (hustle harder · manifest it · you're enough · five easy steps · new year new you), thousands of them, all real clippings. One line of clear water at the horizon: 'Come to me, all of you who are weary.' The only sentence that isn't chopped.
7b990f1597ea785d36a8284c7e0ce90e.jpg.where: Full page — one of the strongest single images available to us

7b9a822b23fbeb075981bb51d3141793.jpg.what: Musgrave Pencil Co. — a 1960s trade catalogue page: each pencil photographed flat, numbered, deadpan specs
7b9a822b23fbeb075981bb51d3141793.jpg.mech: The catalogue's flatness IS the charm. Numbered SKUs, no hierarchy, complete confidence the object deserves documentation.
7b9a822b23fbeb075981bb51d3141793.jpg.ours: 'INSTRUMENTS OF RECORD' — the writing tools of scripture as a specimen page: No. 1 THE FINGER (wrote on stone — Exodus 31:18, and on a wall — Daniel 5:5) · No. 2 THE IRON PEN (Job 19:24 — 'engraved forever in the rock') · No. 3 THE REED PEN (3 John 13) · No. 4 THE STYLUS (Isaiah 8:1). Deadpan specs for each. Ends: No. 5 — YOURS. See page 43.
7b9a822b23fbeb075981bb51d3141793.jpg.where: Near the notebook page — the field guide series

7bf45d9cae72b35a4dc16b0ee880f4b7.jpg.what: 'Reportage des Matchs' — a fluoro-red riso newsprint poster-paper, halftone photos, type running along ruled paths
7bf45d9cae72b35a4dc16b0ee880f4b7.jpg.mech: One shocking ink on grey stock; the rules and angled type make the page feel urgent and handmade at once.
7bf45d9cae72b35a4dc16b0ee880f4b7.jpg.ours: The Spine's alternate print treatment: one fluoro ink (our coral) on uncoated grey, halftone photos of ordinary places, headlines running along the fold lines. If PrintNewspaper.com offers a spot-colour section, THIS is what the removable section should feel like — a different paper inside the paper.

7c149e92660eb5052d153c63f32c4206.jpg.what: Kellogg's PEP Rocket Rings — FREE! at no extra cost, 12 rings of the future, wear 'em collect 'em swap 'em
7c149e92660eb5052d153c63f32c4206.jpg.mech: The prize inside ordinary breakfast. 'No money! No waiting!' — the surprise is already in the box you were buying anyway.
7c149e92660eb5052d153c63f32c4206.jpg.ours: 'ONE IN EVERY COPY' — the paper announces its own prize like a cereal box: somewhere in every issue is one verse meant for the person holding it. 'No money. No waiting. Already inside.' The ad teaches readers HOW to read us — the treasure is standard equipment (2 Corinthians 4:7 — treasure in clay jars).

7f34d39978b870dc04c4687f75c3bd54.jpg.what: Teenage Stepdad 'STOP MONETIZING EVERYTHING' — a perfect vintage toy circular whose every ad begs the same sentence
7f34d39978b870dc04c4687f75c3bd54.jpg.mech: One message wearing forty different commercial costumes. The repetition through changing formats is the joke and the sermon.
7f34d39978b870dc04c4687f75c3bd54.jpg.ours: 'IT IS FINISHED' — a toy-catalogue page where every product panel, starburst, price tag and testimonial says the same three words in different furniture (John 19:30). The gospel repeated through commerce's own costumes until the costume gives up. Risky, funny, deeply on-message: you cannot buy it, it's already paid.

81egnibeitl-sy466.jpg.what: 'Once in a House on Fire' — a real matchbook as the book cover, matches unstruck, the title in a smoke-shaped thought bubble
81egnibeitl-sy466.jpg.mech: One object photographed straight; the drawing completes what the object implies. Nothing else on the cover.
81egnibeitl-sy466.jpg.ours: Already concepted as the stone-with-ladder cover. This original confirms the recipe: REAL object (a stone), one drawn continuation (the stairway as a pencil line rising off it), title in the drawn element. Also the Isaiah 42:3 version: a photographed matchbook with every match struck except one — 'he will not put out a flickering candle.'

84675c397d4591745936da58450c2187.jpg.what: NYT 'Scratch' — Nostalgia, Inc.: a whole page hand-drawn AND hand-written, quotes floating around a painted portrait and shopfront
84675c397d4591745936da58450c2187.jpg.mech: Journalism drawn instead of photographed. The handwriting makes the quotes feel spoken; the clutter is the subject's world.
84675c397d4591745936da58450c2187.jpg.ours: 'THE STONE ROLLER' — our first real profile, drawn this way: somebody ordinary who does one faithful thing (the man who unlocks the church at 6am · the woman who drives four people every Sunday). Hand-drawn portrait, their actual words hand-written around them, their clutter lovingly itemised. Real person, real quotes, zero photography. THIS is how BTS does profiles without stock images.

84b4a6329499b9b3cd3aa30bacb05dfa.jpg.what: 'LUCKY GRAB BAG 99¢' — mystery merchandise, 'some formerly up to $10', a coupon and a pile of drawn objects
84b4a6329499b9b3cd3aa30bacb05dfa.jpg.mech: The mystery bag: you don't choose the contents, and that's the appeal. The itemised pile teases without promising.
84b4a6329499b9b3cd3aa30bacb05dfa.jpg.ours: 'THE PROVIDENCE BAG' — a drawn pile of what people actually got when they didn't get what they prayed for: a closed door (that saved them) · a delay (that rerouted them) · a no (that was a better yes). 'Contents selected for you. Some formerly worth everything.' Romans 8:28 as a grab-bag ad — what you get is chosen, not chosen BY you.

863465deb791871c3567a99935af731c.jpg.what: 'A Gentle Reminder' p81 — a book page where a previous reader's four highlighter colours and red underlines do the arguing
863465deb791871c3567a99935af731c.jpg.mech: Multiple highlight colours = multiple readings, or one reader at different times. The page carries its own history of being needed.
863465deb791871c3567a99935af731c.jpg.ours: 'THE PSALM EVERYBODY MARKED' — Psalm 23 printed once, carrying four readers' marks in four colours, with a small key: yellow = read at a funeral · pink = taped to a hospital bed · blue = memorised at eight years old · green = came back to it last week. Same text, four lives. The key row makes it a testimony page without a single testimony written out.
863465deb791871c3567a99935af731c.jpg.where: Full page — Reading section or Spine

8672e62892dca2ba088e5b6216db675c.jpg.what: Volkskrant magazine — a train-route feature where a huge red sketch and a hand-drawn route with white station names ride OVER the typeset columns
8672e62892dca2ba088e5b6216db675c.jpg.mech: Two layers refusing to merge: rigid columns underneath, one loose drawing over the top. The route connects the whole spread.
8672e62892dca2ba088e5b6216db675c.jpg.ours: The Reading redesigned as this: Genesis 28 set clean in columns, and OVER it one continuous hand-drawn white line — Beersheba to Haran — with the stops lettered by hand where they fall. The drawn journey literally crosses the typeset text, the way the night crossed his plans.

8978078dccf1456bd95e9413da780f94.jpg.what: Dieter Rams 'Good design is' — numbered single words huge in red, the explanations tiny beside them
8978078dccf1456bd95e9413da780f94.jpg.mech: The list IS the poster; the fine print exists but nobody needs it. One adjective per number.
8978078dccf1456bd95e9413da780f94.jpg.ours: 'GOOD NEWS IS' — ten numbered words, huge: 1 free. 2 early. 3 uninvited. 4 patient. 5 specific. 6 unearned. 7 stubborn. 8 quiet. 9 finished. 10 for you. Each with a tiny gloss + verse beside it (finished — John 19:30 · early — Luke 15:20, he ran while the son was far off · stubborn — Lam 3:22). Rams's authority format carrying the actual announcement.

880849f876debfb6dae09b9fbe03667c.jpg.what: 1970s skatepark membership cards — photos, member numbers, signatures, every park its own card
880849f876debfb6dae09b9fbe03667c.jpg.mech: The laminated card proves you belonged somewhere once. Number, photo, signature: identity as ephemera.
880849f876debfb6dae09b9fbe03667c.jpg.ours: 'MEMBER IN GOOD STANDING' — a page of drawn membership cards for the communion of the unqualified: THE DOUBTERS CLUB (member: Thomas, No. 1) · RUNAWAYS ASSOCIATION (Jacob, lifetime member) · DENIERS LOCAL 3 (Peter, reinstated) · latecomers welcome (the 11th-hour workers, Matt 20:9). One blank card at the bottom, your name line empty, marked ALREADY APPROVED.

90b8178b6bec00ab0a9f2a886fc087a9.jpg.what: Levi's 'Now Is Our Time' — a full ad of nothing but hand-painted questions on a brick wall
90b8178b6bec00ab0a9f2a886fc087a9.jpg.mech: Interrogative advertising: the brand asks instead of claims, painted like it was done overnight.
90b8178b6bec00ab0a9f2a886fc087a9.jpg.ours: The wall of questions Jesus actually asked, painted the same way: 'WHO DO YOU SAY I AM? · WHY ARE YOU AFRAID? · DO YOU WANT TO GET WELL? · WHAT DO YOU WANT ME TO DO FOR YOU?' No answers, no product, small footer: he asked more questions than he answered. Between Sundays, page 16.
90b8178b6bec00ab0a9f2a886fc087a9.jpg.where: House ad or the questions page treatment

90be7481734254886cd1f27cbf98a625.jpg.what: The Design Council's 'THE BIG PAPER' — a broadsheet for primary schools, giant multicoloured nameplate, earnest columns
90be7481734254886cd1f27cbf98a625.jpg.mech: A serious institution making a paper for children without talking down: big type, real articles.
90be7481734254886cd1f27cbf98a625.jpg.ours: Evidence for a BTS KIDS EDITION — same chassis, bigger type, the same stories told at eight-year-old level (the Source Rule already forces 5th-grade clarity; this just goes two grades further). Parking it as a future product with this as the visual control.

927cc0e92d6a9aae97be19aa0a221f8b.jpg.what: 'HAVE YOU SEEN MY JACKET?? NOW YOU HAVE' — a lost-poster parody with tear-off tabs, photographed mid-tear
927cc0e92d6a9aae97be19aa0a221f8b.jpg.mech: The lost-pet format flipped into an announcement; the tabs make strangers participants.
927cc0e92d6a9aae97be19aa0a221f8b.jpg.ours: 'HAVE YOU SEEN THIS SHEEP?' — a lost poster for the one out of ninety-nine, tabs at the bottom. Each tab reads FOUND (Luke 15:5-6 — he carries it home rejoicing). Print it as a real page AND as an actual flyer churches can photocopy and staple to poles — the paper's first out-of-paper artifact.

9353378ea51ccd8bdc57d9245a9d3132.jpg.what: Draplin Design Co. Official Merch Store — orange handbill, halftone products, 'If we don't have it, you don't need it', FREE ADVICE / TRUST US!
9353378ea51ccd8bdc57d9245a9d3132.jpg.mech: House merch sold with self-aware carnival confidence; the FREE ADVICE box is the wink that makes the rest land.
9353378ea51ccd8bdc57d9245a9d3132.jpg.ours: The BTS SUPPLY CO. (p41) in its final form — this is the visual control the page has been circling: halftone product cuts, item numbers (BTS-001 THE STONE), the slogan flipped: 'If we don't have it, you don't need it' becomes 'IF WE DON'T SELL IT, IT'S BECAUSE IT'S FREE.' And the FREE ADVICE box becomes FREE GRACE — no email required, TRUST US → Ephesians 2:8 written out.
9353378ea51ccd8bdc57d9245a9d3132.jpg.where: Page 41 final control + real BTS merch page later

943c570f78d0b1757ff36413132bf54f.jpg.what: DesignMantic 'Rule of Thirds' — where viewers look first, with percentages
943c570f78d0b1757ff36413132bf54f.jpg.ours: Workspace craft note, not a page. Filed to the design-dna doc: put the one loud thing on a third-line, and the 41% corner is where the verse goes.
943c570f78d0b1757ff36413132bf54f.jpg.skipwhy: Craft heuristic for us, not content for readers

95da82a881e63d3f86161eb6c1011b3d.jpg.what: Microsoft 'On imagine' — a real métro platform photo with white line-drawn people imagined into it
95da82a881e63d3f86161eb6c1011b3d.jpg.mech: The drawing shows what could be there; the photo grounds it in a real place. Imagination rendered as overlay.
95da82a881e63d3f86161eb6c1011b3d.jpg.ours: Control for 'What else was in the room' (p44, already concepted): photograph the ordinary place, draw the unseen in one continuous white line — the ramp, the traffic of Genesis 28:12, the army of 2 Kings 6:17. This original proves the technique reads instantly at full-page scale.

960be2d0e29caff964ecc1f52ee53a95.jpg.what: Hubba Bubba 'Gumfighting Do's and Don'ts' — a full comic-book page teaching a fake discipline with total rigor: numbered drills, labelled stance diagram, 'your size is not important'
960be2d0e29caff964ecc1f52ee53a95.jpg.mech: Fake expertise formatted as real instruction. The labelled diagram (elbows akimbo, 93°) is the engine.
960be2d0e29caff964ecc1f52ee53a95.jpg.ours: 'PRAYER: A FIELD MANUAL' — the same deadpan instructional rigor for the thing nobody needs instructions for: THE PROPER STANCE (any) · equipment (none) · eyes (open or shut — Nehemiah prayed mid-sentence to a king, 2:4) · YOUR SIZE IS NOT IMPORTANT (the mustard seed drill, Matt 17:20) · ACCEPT NO SUBSTITUTES (vain repetition, Matt 6:7). Funny, and every caption is doctrine.

9702f961e20e5a91231a90f3d514ad8b.jpg.what: 'Don't forget the little good things' — hand-lettered white list on flat blue, starred items
9702f961e20e5a91231a90f3d514ad8b.jpg.mech: A plain list of small mercies; the flat field and handwriting make it feel like a note left for you.
9702f961e20e5a91231a90f3d514ad8b.jpg.ours: 'THE DAILY BREAD LIST' — same treatment on our sky blue: hand-lettered small providences (a parking spot when late · the text back · sleep that came · the kettle · a door held). Header small at the foot: 'Every good gift is from above — James 1:17.' The everyday itemised as provision. Tear-out size so it goes on a fridge.
9702f961e20e5a91231a90f3d514ad8b.jpg.where: Quarter or half page — near Home (p38)

9a004872e5ed6f1b0afd0856a9a942a0.jpg.what: 'The weekend did nothing. Again.' — six drawn panels, six kinds of rest (physical, mental, emotional, social, sensory, creative)
9a004872e5ed6f1b0afd0856a9a942a0.jpg.mech: A taxonomy in hand-drawn panels; the caption admits the reader's exact frustration before helping.
9a004872e5ed6f1b0afd0856a9a942a0.jpg.ours: 'WHY SUNDAY DIDN'T FIX IT' — six panels of rest the Bible actually names: sleep (Ps 127:2, he gives it) · sabbath (Mark 2:27, made for man) · quiet (Ps 46:10) · company (Ecc 4:9-10) · solitude (Mark 1:35, before dawn, alone) · rest for the soul (Matt 11:29 — 'you will find rest for your souls'). The admission stays: one day off only ever gave you one of these.

9a937ac8be96eefa3cc0a98e1058b33d.jpg.what: A Rumi line set large, with photographed objects (keys, coffee, strawberries, a fig, a log) sitting between the words like rebus pieces
9a937ac8be96eefa3cc0a98e1058b33d.jpg.mech: The objects slow the sentence down: you read at walking pace because things keep interrupting, pleasantly.
9a937ac8be96eefa3cc0a98e1058b33d.jpg.ours: Psalm 23 set this way — 'The LORD is my shepherd' with the actual objects between phrases: green pastures (a tuft of grass) · still waters (a glass of water) · a table (a fork) · oil (a small bottle) · a cup running over. Every noun in the psalm photographed as an ordinary household object. The most famous poem in the world, re-read at walking pace.
9a937ac8be96eefa3cc0a98e1058b33d.jpg.where: Full page — Reading section or poster

9af6190b1f265e6c5d4c2c1d245dd7a1.jpg.what: D62 Studio '1950s Retro Ads' — a template pack advertising itself with starbursts and spokespeople
9af6190b1f265e6c5d4c2c1d245dd7a1.jpg.mech: A style guide for the whole vintage-ad genre in one sheet.
9af6190b1f265e6c5d4c2c1d245dd7a1.jpg.ours: Not a page — a STYLE ATLAS for all our ad parodies (Free Store, Supply Co, mail-order, coupons). Keep as the swipe file that keeps our fake ads period-correct instead of vaguely retro.
9af6190b1f265e6c5d4c2c1d245dd7a1.jpg.where: Style reference for the ad-parody family
9af6190b1f265e6c5d4c2c1d245dd7a1.jpg.skipwhy: Template pack — style reference, not content

9b664df307cea8b429d0313ea4883ff8.jpg.what: Urgent/important 2x2 — DO IT NOW · PLAN IT · DELEGATE · DROP IT
9b664df307cea8b429d0313ea4883ff8.jpg.ours: Workspace only. In the paper it would make us productivity coaches — the constitution says no.
9b664df307cea8b429d0313ea4883ff8.jpg.skipwhy: Self-optimisation framework; not the paper's voice

9c45f1c1139375b2169110898e1b418f.jpg.what: 'Things I Can Control' — one drawn remote, each button labelled with what's actually yours
9c45f1c1139375b2169110898e1b418f.jpg.mech: One familiar object turned into a diagram of agency. The joke: the remote controls almost nothing, and neither do you.
9c45f1c1139375b2169110898e1b418f.jpg.ours: 'THE REMOTE' — same drawn object, our labels: what the buttons actually do (my next sentence · who I tell · whether I go back · what I do with today) and, printed on the casing where the brand goes: THE REST IS NOT A BUTTON — 'Can all your worries add a single moment to your life?' (Matt 6:27). Pairs with the in-my-control loop already concepted; pick ONE of the two.
9c45f1c1139375b2169110898e1b418f.jpg.where: Near Weather (p20) — choose between this and the loop

9d5b11237f87093ce241ca21805ea16e.jpg.what: 'Hi You!' — a full handwritten letter to a struggling reader, every other phrase highlighted in different colours
9d5b11237f87093ce241ca21805ea16e.jpg.mech: The letter format plus highlighter = somebody wrote this AND somebody marked the parts that mattered. Double intimacy.
9d5b11237f87093ce241ca21805ea16e.jpg.ours: Control for the marked-up page family — but this one earns its OWN page: 'A LETTER TO THE ONE WHO ALMOST DIDN'T PICK THIS UP.' Handwritten, warm, honest about how hard it is to say 'not fine', highlighted through. Every highlighted claim footed with a tiny verse ref (so many people waiting — Rom 12:15 · you're not on your own — Gen 28:15 · the world is waiting for you — Jer 29:11). The paper's front-door letter, page 03.

9d8fc33c6d6d7e831e2b35b37e44762a.jpg.what: 'How to do the Stumble' — a zine teaching a dance move in 9 numbered photos and deadpan steps, skill level: INTERMEDIATE-RISKY
9d8fc33c6d6d7e831e2b35b37e44762a.jpg.mech: Physical instruction photographed frame by frame; the grid of tiny repeated figures IS the page.
9d8fc33c6d6d7e831e2b35b37e44762a.jpg.ours: 'HOW TO COME BACK: A STEP GUIDE' — the prodigal's walk home taught like a dance manual: 9 drawn frames (stand up in the pigpen · rehearse the speech · start walking · keep walking · see the house · get seen first · get run at · drop the speech · get hugged mid-sentence). SKILL LEVEL: NONE REQUIRED. TIME: while he was still a long way off. Luke 15 as choreography.
9d8fc33c6d6d7e831e2b35b37e44762a.jpg.where: Full page — the funnest deep page we could run

9f28f0fd890c5a3c7bd1f54f195b9107.jpg.t: The torn photo, finished in pen
9f28f0fd890c5a3c7bd1f54f195b9107.jpg.what: A photo of a park fence torn away mid-frame, the missing half completed in ballpoint on paper, date-stamped
9f28f0fd890c5a3c7bd1f54f195b9107.jpg.mech: Half real, half remembered. The tear line is honest about where the record stops and the drawing begins.
9f28f0fd890c5a3c7bd1f54f195b9107.jpg.ours: 'WHAT THE CAMERA MISSED' — for the photo essay: each ordinary-place photograph torn along one edge, the missing portion completed in ink with what the text claims was also there (the stairway continuing off-frame, Gen 28:12). The tear admits we cannot photograph it; the pen refuses to leave it out. Date-stamp each one like evidence.
9f28f0fd890c5a3c7bd1f54f195b9107.jpg.where: Page 44 treatment — sits beside the white-line overlay option

9f87acfe365e6c8459f146eca38a5ec2.jpg.what: 'Hey Tweens, Watch This!' — a contents spread where every entry is a tilted ticket with a numbered dot, giant word behind
9f87acfe365e6c8459f146eca38a5ec2.jpg.mech: The index as confetti: each item a physical ticket you could pick up, page numbers as badges.
9f87acfe365e6c8459f146eca38a5ec2.jpg.ours: Contents (p02) alternate: every section of the paper as a scattered ticket stub — THE READING p07 · WEATHER p20 · BUT GOD p33 — tossed across the page around the giant word BETWEEN. Admission: free. One ticket left blank: 'whatever page you open first — that one was for you.'

a010fb4b88d59838292df6b14123fa4c.jpg.what: 'BE A LIFE BOAT' — one drawn boat, hand-lettered functions radiating: a second chance, a safe place in a storm, hand them the rope
a010fb4b88d59838292df6b14123fa4c.jpg.mech: One object as a job description, radiating verbs.
a010fb4b88d59838292df6b14123fa4c.jpg.ours: Already concepted as BE A STONE. This original adds the verb energy: keep the radiating lines as IMPERATIVES (be somewhere to rest a head · be proof it happened · be the start of a house). Two objects could run as a series: BE A STONE / BE A DOOR (John 10:9).

a01bb2dd7bfb3b2e2f8d28539bd6e2ce.jpg.what: IGA 'Jokers Wild' — a grocery page whose top half is a card game: play your cards against this chart, thousands still to be won
a01bb2dd7bfb3b2e2f8d28539bd6e2ce.jpg.mech: The store invents a GAME to make you come back weekly; the chart of winning sequences is the hook.
a01bb2dd7bfb3b2e2f8d28539bd6e2ce.jpg.ours: 'COME BACK NEXT WEEK' — the mechanic behind our whole issue cadence, made literal once: a collect-the-verses card across issues (Issue 001 carries Gen 28:15, Issue 002 carries the next promise…), a chart showing the 'winning sequence' is just the same promise repeated through scripture. No prizes to buy — 'no purchase required' is the theology. Also simply: our coupons page learns the RETURN visit.

a191c76600d8401b9c2519b2a564ca23.jpg.what: 'Thinking Maps' — eight diagram types matched to eight thinking processes
a191c76600d8401b9c2519b2a564ca23.jpg.ours: Workspace craft reference for the field-guide pages (which map type fits which passage). Not a reader-facing page.
a191c76600d8401b9c2519b2a564ca23.jpg.skipwhy: Classroom tool; useful to us, not to readers

a1858c8ea0b1818be501d9679b39bf85.jpg.what: 'Positive Energy Journaling' — wellness prompts on sage green
a1858c8ea0b1818be501d9679b39bf85.jpg.ours: Skip: the voice is self-sourced positivity, which is exactly what our notebook page (p43) is NOT — ours asks one question and points at a verse, not at your energy. Kept only as a contrast reference.
a1858c8ea0b1818be501d9679b39bf85.jpg.skipwhy: Wellness-journaling voice conflicts with the constitution

a1d71467c2353176f17b66ab1c503a82.jpg.t: The drawn person in the real room
a1d71467c2353176f17b66ab1c503a82.jpg.what: A photographed café bench with a line-drawn cut-out girl sitting on it, speech bubble about hitting the Instagram stories limit
a1d71467c2353176f17b66ab1c503a82.jpg.mech: The drawn character inhabits the real photo; the paper cut-out edge makes her deliberately artificial. Comic meets documentary.
a1d71467c2353176f17b66ab1c503a82.jpg.ours: 'THE FRIEND WHO ISN'T THERE YET' — for the modern-parallel page: real photographed places (bus seat, kitchen chair, pew end) with one drawn cut-out figure sitting in them, speech-bubbling the things people actually think ('everyone else seems fine'). Final frame: the same seat, drawn figure gone, real light on it — 'you were never the only one in the room.' Genesis 28:16 as the caption.

a573827050edf313cd05b87dddb97fa4.jpg.mech: One big word decomposed into small human traits; the drop-lines make the word a roof over its people.
a573827050edf313cd05b87dddb97fa4.jpg.ours: 'CHURCH' — the giant word, and hanging from its letters the actual people: the one who unlocks at 6am · the one who drives four others · the one who can't sing but stands anyway · the one who came back after 9 years · the one still deciding in the car park. Under it: 'you are living stones — 1 Peter 2:5.' The word means the people, not the building; the diagram makes that argument without a sentence.

a7c8c21f302daec86a0b034f585f83d0.jpg.ours: Evidence for THE BTS ANNUAL — our brain (constitution, DNA, decisions, postmortems) printed once a year as a slim newsprint zine for the team and future collaborators. THE WORRY (not visible, always packed — 1 Peter 5:7, 'give all your worries to God, for he cares about you'). One callout line points at empty space. That's the page.

ad2a4fde1e2cf7e832e3350883147deb.jpg.mech: Cartography with personality: the map is inviting because it's clearly one person's hand.
ad2a4fde1e2cf7e832e3350883147deb.jpg.ours: 'THE NEIGHBORHOODS OF THE STORY' — Genesis 28's world drawn as this kind of map (Beersheba's family drama district · the open country where nothing is named · Luz, pop. asleep · Bethel, renamed overnight · the long road to Haran with mile doodles). OR the local version: YOUR town hand-mapped with the ordinary places God showed up for readers — submitted via the postbox card. Both sourced.

b4a44552dc57ca0267b13600a86ce755.jpg.what: 'A tu Vuelta' — a walking figure on a horizon, the road behind him built entirely from handwritten text narrowing to the vanishing point
b4a44552dc57ca0267b13600a86ce755.jpg.mech: The text IS the road: perspective built from sentences, the figure walking on his own story.
b4a44552dc57ca0267b13600a86ce755.jpg.ours: THE COVER CANDIDATE to beat: one small figure walking a road that is Genesis 28 handwritten, narrowing behind him to Beersheba at the vanishing point. Every step is on the words. Title small in the sky: I AM WITH YOU. This and the cut-strip stairway are the two strongest cover ideas we now hold — same theology, two crafts.

Every card tearable in spirit — this page becomes phone wallpapers for free later.

YOU PAY: nothing (it's been paid — John 19:30). The order coupon is our postbox card again. Strong sibling of the FREE STORE; run ONE of them per issue.

c2b5555532d95992ef057a1f9dfdcb37.jpg.what: Bristol Jazz Festival 2024 — a fold-out programme as a newspaper: FRIDAY rotated huge on the fold, acts gridded with photos and times
c2b5555532d95992ef057a1f9dfdcb37.jpg.mech: The day-name as monument type; the grid hangs off it. A schedule made monumental.
c2b5555532d95992ef057a1f9dfdcb37.jpg.ours: THE WEEK, MONUMENTAL — our Spine redesigned with day-names at this scale: TUESDAY rotated huge up the fold, and hanging off it the small real things of a Tuesday with their verses. The ordinary day treated like a headline act — which is the entire thesis of Between Sundays.

c61d83513e2d80461bd15a388336a58a.jpg.what: A zine spread — 'TWO WAYS TO PRINT SOME REAL NEWSPAPER FEEL' with tipped-in samples and taped notes
c61d83513e2d80461bd15a388336a58a.jpg.mech: Production talk shown, not hidden: the paper explains its own making with samples taped in.
c61d83513e2d80461bd15a388336a58a.jpg.ours: 'HOW THIS PAPER GOT MADE' — a colophon page done as a scrapbook: the stock, the inks, the press, a taped-in swatch of the actual newsprint, the printer's name, what it cost per copy (real number). Transparency as brand: nothing hidden, everything sourced — including us (the two humans + three machines note lives here).

c688cf95323b7717711d0379ca274eee.jpg.what: 'How to Respond to Emotions' — a 2-axis field (energy × comfort), feelings plotted, one verb per quadrant
c688cf95323b7717711d0379ca274eee.jpg.mech: Feelings become coordinates; each quadrant gets one instruction.
c688cf95323b7717711d0379ca274eee.jpg.ours: 'WHERE ARE YOU ON THIS PAGE?' — same two axes, but the quadrant verbs are David's: high-energy discomfort → CRY OUT (Ps 13) · low-energy discomfort → BE STILL (Ps 46:10) · high-energy pleasure → SING (Ps 98:1) · low-energy pleasure → GIVE THANKS (Ps 136:1). Every plotted feeling is a psalm number, because there is genuinely a psalm at every coordinate. The Psalter as an emotional map — no wellness language required.

c9d95025bc19a18dcc56e3595ff899db.jpg.mech: A brand letting its own hand show: annotations ON the layout make it feel owned, not produced.
c9d95025bc19a18dcc56e3595ff899db.jpg.ours: The energy our social/web presence should carry — the paper photographed, then scribbled on: a circle around one verse, an arrow, 'read this one first' in marker. Digital wrapper for print product. Feeds Grow's platform playbook, not an issue page.
